full_details: At nine you rehearsed the old Hamlet. Garnish set a handful of flour, not a bag, and nobody wrote in the book. You waited Pope's word on the second turn. Nick kept four lines. At home you washed the hand that eats. The hair went back as it was. Dinner was threepence. At two you played the Ghost. You came off with the flour still in. At twenty past five a christening was coming out at St Helen's. Gossips, a cake-basket, a nurse, the child roaring. She was last down the step, in dark green, and the latch caught her sleeve. You freed it. Her gloved hand rested on yours a moment. She looked at the ink on your finger. She said, you are the one that writes. You said Mistress. She went after the others. At forty past nine you said she knew you by your hand, and that it is not safe. You put a small cross in the almanac. No name beside it.
one_sentence: You played the Ghost with a handful of flour still in your hair, freed a dark green sleeve at the porch, and marked the day with a cross.
title: Played the Ghost in flour, and marked a cross
